chunks: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He wills to create a being, He gathers every form between him and Adam, then creates him upon the form of one of them. So no one should ever say to his child, 'This one does not resemble me, nor does he resemble anything from my forefathers.'

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam عليه السلام, the first human ancestor
key_terms.اَللَّهَ: Allah, the Creator whose will determines creation
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted, an expression of divine majesty and transcendence
key_terms.صُورَةٍ: form or likeness, referring to inherited appearance
key_terms.يَخْلُقَ: to create, referring to Allah’s act of bringing a human into existence

ai.seo_question: Why might a child not resemble his father or immediate ancestors according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that human resemblance is tied to the many forms present in one's lineage back to Adam عليه السلام. It discourages denying familial resemblance in children and points to Allah’s power and wisdom in creation.
